core_obligations: Affine case: write the affine formal algebraic space as a filtered colimit of affine schemes with thickenings as transition morphisms, note that all stages have the same reduction, and read off representability and the thickening property for the morphism from that reduction (proof lines 2840-2849).
Affine case: supply the verification of the universal property, which the author declines to prove here and reduces to four cited statements (proof lines 2849-2854).

Global case, identification step: for two members of the affine presentation show that the fibre product of the reduction of one with the other is etale over that reduction, hence reduced, so that the projection factors through the reduction of the other, and conclude the three-way identification of the fibre products (proof lines 2856-2871).

Global case, quotient step: set up the two projections from the disjoint union of these fibre products to the disjoint union of the reductions, note that they form an etale equivalence relation, and obtain the quotient algebraic space X_red by the presentation theorem (proof lines 2872-2879).

Global case, transfer step: observe that the comparison diagram between the presentations is cartesian, transfer representability of the morphism to X along the surjective etale morphism using a bootstrap lemma, and transfer the thickening property using a descent lemma for representable transformations and the equivalence of thickenings with surjective closed immersions (proof lines 2879-2890).

Universal property in general: for a morphism from a reduced algebraic space, note that the fibre products with the members of the presentation are etale over a reduced source and hence reduced, so they factor through the reductions, and conclude by the fact that they form an etale covering of the source (proof lines 2892-2907).
proof_roadmap: Affine case: reduction of a filtered colimit of thickenings (proof lines 2840-2849).
Affine case: the universal property, left to the reader with four pointers (proof lines 2849-2854).
Global case: identification of the pairwise fibre products (proof lines 2856-2871).
Global case: etale equivalence relation and quotient (proof lines 2872-2879).
Global case: transfer of representability and of the thickening property (proof lines 2879-2890).
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, for a formal algebraic space X over a scheme, a reduced algebraic space X_red together with a representable morphism to X which is a thickening, and asserts that morphisms from a reduced algebraic space into X factor uniquely through it (statement lines 2832-2838). The proof has three parts. The affine case is settled by writing the affine formal algebraic space as a filtered colimit of affine schemes whose transition morphisms are thickenings, so that all stages have isomorphic reductions; representability and the thickening property follow from the covering-by-thickenings lemma and from closure of thickenings under composition, and the author explicitly leaves the verification of the universal property to the reader, pointing at the four statements that make it routine (proof lines 2840-2854). The global case is a glueing construction: for the chosen affine presentation of X one takes the reductions of the members, observes that the fibre products of a reduction with a member are etale over that reduction and therefore reduced, so that the projections factor through the reductions of the members, identifies the resulting fibre products in three ways, and concludes that the two projections form an etale equivalence relation whose quotient is an algebraic space by the presentation theorem; the comparison diagram with the presentation is cartesian, and representability and the thickening property of the resulting morphism are then transferred along a surjective etale morphism by a bootstrap lemma and a descent lemma for representable transformations (proof lines 2856-2890). The third part proves the universal property in general: for a morphism from a reduced algebraic space, the fibre products with the members of the presentation are etale over the source and hence reduced, so each factors through the corresponding reduction, and since those fibre products form an etale covering of the source, the morphism itself factors through X_red (proof lines 2892-2907). The claim is H3: the affine computation, the equivalence-relation glueing with its three-way identification, the transfer of representability and of the thickening property along a cover, and the general universal property are four independent pieces of work.
